chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

It is upon the Imam to bring out those imprisoned for debt on the day of الجمعة prayer for الجمعة prayer, and on the day of the ʿEid for the ʿEid. Then he should send someone with them, and when they have completed the salat and the ʿEid, he should return them to the prison.

key_terms.الدَّيْنِ: debt for which the imprisonment has occurred
key_terms.السِّجْنِ: the prison to which they are returned afterward
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer they are taken out to perform
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the lawful authority responsible for implementing this ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking debt prisoners out for Friday and ʿEid prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal duty of the Imam regarding those imprisoned for debt: they are to be brought out to attend الجمعة and ʿEid prayer under supervision. After completing the salat and ʿEid observance, they are to be returned to prison, showing both the enforcement of legal custody and the preservation of communal worship rights.
